question.text: Under Hindu Succession Act 1956, a daughter has:

answer.text: Equal coparcenary rights to ancestral property as a son
Rights only if mentioned in the Will
Rights only to the mother's property

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended by the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, a daughter is recognised as a coparcener in a joint Hindu family governed by Mitakshara law and has the same rights and liabilities in ancestral property as a son, including the right to claim partition. This position has been reaffirmed by the Supreme Court in subsequent rulings. The Trap: Option A reflects the pre-2005 position and is no longer correct. Option C confuses testamentary succession (rights under a Will) with statutory coparcenary rights. Option D incorrectly limits a daughter's inheritance to maternal property alone. Note: The cited Retirement Adviser workbook pages list the Hindu Succession Act among applicable personal succession laws but do not, in the pages reviewed, spell out the 2005 amendment or the coparcenary-rights language. The framing above reflects current Indian succession law and case law rather than a direct workbook citation.
